answer: most convincing defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed job publishes a signed record whose nonce hashes the previous one, so reputation is one unbroken voyage of verifiable work. An attacker cannot fork a trusted identity into parallel copies, because forking replays the same nonce chain and duplicate chain heads are rejected as invalid. Each fake identity must start at zero and honestly earn trust, while the system stays open like a meadow any newcomer may enter. The attacker's cost is paying real compute for real work many times over, like a sable
